messages.subject: Re: initPackrat fails
messages.body_plain:
RODBC 1.3-10 is current, so Packrat won't be able to find binaries for 1.3-9 and is likely trying to install RODBC from source, but failing to compile the sources. Trying to build and install manually will probably make the error visible; try this:

1. In packrat.sources/RODBC, you'll find a .tar.gz file with the source for RODBC 1.3-9. Decompress it to a temporary folder.
2. Use devtools::install("/temporary folder/RODBC") to install the package.

In all likelihood this package will fail to build or install with a usable error message. When I tried it on my system I got this:

checking for sqlext.h... no
configure: error: "ODBC headers sql.h and sqlext.h not found"
ERROR: configuration failed for package 'RODBC'
* removing '/private/tmp/Rtmp3f6FLX/Rinsteaad8f342a4/RODBC'
      -----------------------------------
ERROR: package installation failed
Error: Command failed (1)

which suggests that RODBC has some nonstandard build dependencies.

We should probably add something to Packrat to make it possible to see these errors; I opened issue #32 to track this.

For a workaround in your particular scenario, you might try either upgrading to RODBC 1.3-10 (for which binaries are readily available and building is therefore unnecessary) as a temporary fix, or configuring your system such that it's able to build RODBC from source.

Jonathan.

messages.subject: Re: Is this useful for deployments?
messages.body_plain:
Packrat will try to hit CRAN if a package came from CRAN, but if it fails to get the package from CRAN, it should fall back on building the package from its cached source (in packrat.sources). If this isn't the behavior you saw, would you mind sharing what output you saw from initPackrat() on the firewalled machine?

You can also force Packrat to bypass CRAN by default (and always build from sources) by setting the option pkgType to "source".

Jonathan.

messages.subject: Re: bootstrap issue: Failed to parse
messages.body_plain:
Run R's parse function on script.R. That should tell you what the parse error is. (Arguably, packrat should show you this error; I've opened issue #36 to suggest that it should.) Once the file parses successfully, you should be able to bootstrap the directory without problems.

If you're seeing problems even after resolving parse errors, here are a couple of next steps:

1) You can indeed add dependencies manually. Do this by creating a "dependencies.R" file in your project directory and adding a require(libraryname) statement for each dependency.
2) If you're willing, post the file that parses in R but not in packrat here so we can investigate further.

Jonathan.

messages.subject: Re: bootstrap issue: Failed to parse
messages.body_plain:
On OSX Mavericks, R will sometimes try to use /usr/bin/gnutar, which was dropped in Mavericks. This appears to be the source of both of the errors you're seeing. You can fix the problem by telling R to use /usr/bin/tar instead. Put this in the .Renviron:

TAR=/usr/bin/tar

Jonathan.
